title: Design authorization for Azure and on-premises resources
learningObjective: Recommend how people and workloads are authorized to Azure resources (RBAC, custom roles, PIM, ABAC) and to on-premises resources (application proxy, Private Access, Domain Services).
foundation: Authorization decides what a signed-in identity may do.
For Azure resources the rule is least privilege: the smallest role, at the smallest scope, for the shortest time.
On-premises apps can use Microsoft Entra ID as their front door too, so remote users get MFA without a traditional VPN.
engineer: Azure RBAC design: assign roles to groups, not users; use built-in roles first; scope at management group, subscription, resource group or resource; create custom roles (Actions/NotActions, DataActions) only when no built-in role fits; avoid Owner and User Access Administrator except for a few, and use the Role Based Access Control Administrator role with conditions to limit which roles others can assign.

Privileged Identity Management (Entra ID P2 or ID Governance): make admin roles eligible rather than permanent, with time-bound activation, MFA, justification, approval and access reviews. Covers Entra roles, Azure roles and groups (PIM for Groups).

Attribute-based access control (ABAC) adds conditions to role assignments, for example Storage Blob Data Reader only for blobs with the index tag Project=Alpha. Data-plane access (Storage Blob Data, Key Vault Secrets User, Cosmos DB data roles) is separate from control-plane roles like Contributor.

On-premises resources: Microsoft Entra application proxy publishes internal web apps (with pre-authentication, Conditional Access, and Kerberos constrained delegation for Windows-integrated apps) through outbound-only connectors. Microsoft Entra Private Access (Global Secure Access) provides Zero Trust network access to private apps on any port, replacing VPNs. Microsoft Entra Domain Services gives a managed domain (LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, Group Policy) for legacy apps moved to Azure, without running domain controllers. Entra Kerberos enables identity-based access to Azure Files for hybrid users.

animation.caption: Choose the right authorization approach for Azure and for on-premises apps.

example.title: Least privilege at a bank
body: Cloud engineers are eligible for Contributor on their landing-zone subscriptions through PIM, activated for 4 hours with justification; Owner requires approval. A custom 'VM Operator' role lets the service desk only start and restart VMs.
The legacy HR intranet is published with application proxy and Conditional Access, so staff reach it from home with MFA and no VPN.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Subscription > Access control (IAM) > Add role assignment; Conditions tab for ABAC.
Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity governance > Privileged Identity Management > Azure resources.
Microsoft Entra admin center > Applications > Enterprise applications > Application proxy.
configuration.cli:
az role definition create --role-definition @vm-operator.json
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id <group-id> --assignee-principal-type Group --role "VM Operator" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/rg-app

lab.objective: Choose how to authorize access in Azure and on-premises.
steps: Answer every case in both trainers.
expected: Application proxy for on-premises web apps

validation.text: Chose the right Azure authorization approach
Chose the right on-premises access solution

failureScenarios: Opening inbound ports for remote access
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: An operator can delete VMs although they should only restart them.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a custom role with only start/restart/read actions.

troubleshooting.symptom: A user is Contributor on a storage account but cannot read blobs with Entra auth.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign a Storage Blob Data role (data plane).

comparisons.difference: RBAC controls who can act; Policy controls what resource configurations are allowed.
Application proxy publishes web apps; Private Access gives network-level Zero Trust access to any private app or port.

misconceptions.myth: Global Administrator can manage all Azure resources by default.
misconceptions.reality: Entra roles and Azure RBAC are separate; Global Admins must elevate access to get User Access Administrator.
Built-in roles are maintained by Microsoft; use custom only when needed.

architectureDecisions: Publish on-premises apps through Entra (application proxy or Private Access) instead of VPN where possible.

verification.notes: Drafted by AI and checked against the linked official documentation. Not yet reviewed by a human subject-matter expert.

walkthrough.subtitle: Give exactly the access that is needed, only when it is needed — in Azure and on-premises.

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Too many people have too much access
body: Owner everywhere is easy and dangerous. Design so each person gets only what they need.

steps.label: RBAC
steps.title: Role + scope, assigned to a group
body: Pick the narrowest built-in role, assign it to a group, at the smallest scope (resource group rather than subscription). Create a custom role only if no built-in role fits.

steps.label: PIM
steps.title: Admin rights only when needed
body: Privileged Identity Management makes roles 'eligible'. Admins activate them for a few hours, with MFA, a reason and sometimes approval.

steps.label: Conditions
steps.title: Finer control with ABAC
body: Conditions on a role assignment can check attributes, for example: may read only blobs tagged Project=Alpha. Remember that reading data needs data roles such as Storage Blob Data Reader; Contributor is not enough.

steps.label: On-premises
steps.title: Entra as the front door for internal apps
body: Application proxy publishes an internal web app through an outbound connector: users sign in with Entra ID and MFA, and no inbound ports open. Private Access does the same for any private app or port, replacing the VPN.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Authorization design
recap: ABAC conditions; data roles for data
Application proxy / Private Access for on-premises

handsOn.title: Create a least-privilege custom role
handsOn.cost: Free. Role definitions and assignments cost nothing.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription. Work in a resource group called rg-az305-lab.
If rg-az305-lab does not exist yet: Resource groups > Create > name rg-az305-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
Open Cloud Shell (Bash) from the portal toolbar.

steps.do: Save your subscription ID in a variable.
steps.code: SUB=$(az account show --query id -o tsv); echo $SUB

steps.do: Create a role definition file that allows only reading, starting and restarting VMs in the lab resource group.
steps.see: No output; the file vm-operator.json exists.
steps.code:
cat > vm-operator.json <<EOF
{
  "Name": "VM Operator (lab)",
  "Description": "Read, start and restart VMs only",
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action"
  ],
  "AssignableScopes": [ "/subscriptions/$SUB/resourceGroups/rg-az305-lab" ]
}
EOF

steps.see: JSON describing the new role, with type CustomRole.

steps.do: In the portal: rg-az305-lab > Access control (IAM) > Roles, search 'VM Operator'.
steps.see: Your custom role listed. Open it > Permissions to see exactly three actions.
steps.tip: Compare with Virtual Machine Contributor, which also allows delete, resize and more.

steps.do: Access control (IAM) > Add > Add role assignment: look at the Conditions tab on a Storage Blob Data role (don't save).
steps.see: The ABAC condition builder (for example filtering by blob index tags).

check: The custom role shows only read, start and restart.
cleanup: Delete the role: az role definition delete --name "VM Operator (lab)"
Resource groups > rg-az305-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete.
